channel.title: Hartford Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Hartford Business Journal (hartfordbusiness.com)

item.title: Shuttered New Britain elementary school targeted for apartment conversion
item.description: A long idle plan to transform a shuttered New Britain elementary school into apartments is picking up steam.

item.title: 🔒 Stanley Black & Decker details layoff timetable for 300 workers
item.description: After announcing last week that it will permanently close its last remaining manufacturing plant in New Britain, toolmaker Stanley Black & Decker this week has provided the state with a specific timetable for layoffs from that facility.

item.title: UHart plans $2.4M outdoor athletics complex named for NBA alumnus Vin Baker
item.description: The project will include six tennis courts, along with a basketball court and lighting for nighttime use.

item.title: 🔒 Van Wilgen’s to open Southington garden center at former Smithland site
item.description: Van Wilgen’s Garden Center plans to open a new retail location in Southington later this month at the site of a former Smithland Pet & Garden Center.

item.title: New Haven’s Union Square redevelopment plan to be showcased in public hearing
item.description: Phase One will include approximately 541 residential units and approximately 31,000 square feet of retail and commercial space.

item.title: 🔒 CT to receive $154M federal grant to improve rural health care access
item.description: Connecticut will receive a $154 million federal grant to help improve health care access and outcomes in rural communities, Gov. Ned Lamont announced Thursday.

item.title: 🔒 Blue Back Square adds tenants, names new property manager; occupancy reaches 99%
item.description: Blue Back Square in West Hartford has added two new tenants and named a new property manager as the mixed-use development continues to expand its retail and wellness offerings.

item.title: Hartford proposes first capital bond issue since 2017 bailout with $50M borrowing plan
item.description: Hartford proposes first capital bond issue since 2017 bailout with $50M borrowing plan

item.title: 🔒 Solar bill draws business support, cost warnings as lawmakers weigh clean energy overhaul
item.description: Connecticut’s major energy companies are backing a proposed overhaul of the state’s clean energy incentive programs — but with strings attached, as they raise concerns about ratepayer costs and program design.

item.title: 🔒 PURA grants UI nearly $68M rate hike, wipes out English Station penalties
item.description: Connecticut’s utility regulator has approved a nearly $68 million rate increase for United Illuminating, granting the electric company that serves the New Haven and Bridgeport areas additional revenue and erasing all financial penalties tied to its failure to clean up a contaminated former power plant.
